import html from typing import Final # Template for rendering a blog post. The placeholders are safe because we escape # the user supplied values before inserting them. BLOG_FORMAT: Final[str] = ( "
\n" "

{title}

\n" "
{body}
\n" "
" ) def render_blog_post(title: str, body: str) -> str: """ Render a blog post for safe display on a web page. Parameters ---------- title : str The user‑supplied title of the blog post. body : str The user‑supplied main content of the blog post. Returns ------- str The fully rendered HTML string with user content safely escaped. Raises ------ ValueError If either title or body is empty or exceeds 10,000 characters. Notes ----- * The function uses :func:`html.escape` to neutralise any HTML, JavaScript or other markup that might be injected by a malicious user. * The rendering template is a constant string; no dynamic formatting beyond the safe placeholders is performed, mitigating CWE‑707 risks. """ # Basic validation to avoid rendering nonsense or excessively large content if not title.strip(): raise ValueError("Title must not be empty.") if not body.strip(): raise ValueError("Body must not be empty.") # Optional: limit size to prevent DoS or excessive memory usage MAX_LENGTH = 10_000 if len(title) > MAX_LENGTH or len(body) > MAX_LENGTH: raise ValueError(f"Title and body must not exceed {MAX_LENGTH} characters.") # Escape user input to neutralise HTML/JS injection safe_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(body, quote=True) # Render the template with sanitized values rendered = BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_title, body=safe_body) return rendered
